Definition: Whether government taxes, customs duties, and other revenue can be paid using the instant digital payment system, indicating integration of payment infrastructure with tax administration systems.
Comments: Revenue collection via digital channels is supported through tax system modernization: Algeria's Directorate-General of Taxes modernization includes online tax filing and online payment via the "Moussahama'tic" portal, enabling government revenue collection digitally (at least for registered users).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Algeria's DGI operates the Jibaya'tic and Moussahama'tic e-portals, enabling online declaration and payment (by CIB/EDAHABIA card) of several tax types (VAT/G50, G12, Taxe de Domiciliation Bancaire) since 2021. Enrolment is voluntary and customs duties are handled separately, so "Partial" (2) remains the correct code.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system enables or plans to enable instant payments across national borders to other countries or regional payment systems, supporting remittances, trade, and regional integration.
Comments: Cross-border payment linkage is developing: the Bank of Algeria officially joined the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS) network (Aug 2025), enabling intra-African cross-border payments/settlement in local currencies through PAPSS (implementation/adoption by banks may still be ramping).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Updated. Bank of Algeria formally joined PAPSS in August 2025 as an 18th country of presence/settlement participant; PAPSS's own June 2026 network coverage map lists Algeria as live, and 2026 analysis confirms settlement-level corridors are operational while individual commercial banks (BNA, BEA, BADR named as most advanced) complete connectivity through 2026. This is beyond "under development" but not yet fully functional across all banks — revised to 4 (Partially functional).

Comments: Evidence indicates G2P via accounts in limited scope: AfricaNenda SIIPS 2024 consumer research notes that "students receive university scholarships via bank accounts," which drives digital payment usage, indicating at least a limited/segment G2P digitization use case.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.

Scattered digitisation exists (scholarships, a pension-status verification app) but G2P remains "Limited Use" (2), not active/systemic.

Definition: Whether the system enables consumer payments to merchants and businesses for goods and services, including retail purchases, bill payments, e-commerce, and subscription services.
Comments: Merchant (P2B) payments are supported via QR code mobile payments: “DZ MOB PAY” is described as enabling payments by scanning QR codes for merchants.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed and updated with fresher data. DZ Mob Pay (launched January 2025, operated by GIE Monétique) enables QR-code merchant payments; by end-2025 it had 14,283 merchant accounts and processed 12,682 QR transactions. Merchant coverage is thin (c.1% of Algeria's ~1.2 million declared merchants) but the P2B use case is confirmed operational — "Yes" (2) confirmed.

Definition: Whether the system enables citizen payments to government for taxes, fees, licenses, fines, utility bills, and other government service charges.
Comments: Person-to-government (P2G) digital payments are part of the national strategy and e-services: a description of Algeria's tax modernization notes online filing and online payment of taxes via the “Moussahama'tic” portal (tax authority), which implies taxpayers can pay government taxes digitally.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Upgraded. The AADL3 social-housing programme made electronic payment (Edahabia/CIB) mandatory with no cash alternative, generating 3.6 million transactions worth 65.27 billion DZD in December 2025 alone; Algeria's state news agency (APS) attributes the 46% surge in 2025 e-payments largely to public administrations' adoption of digital collection, alongside the established Jibaya'tic/Moussahama'tic tax e-payment portals. This is active, high-volume use, not merely limited use — revised to 3 (Yes – Active Use).

Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: The Bank of Algeria states it “monitors and ensures the proper functioning, efficiency and security of payment systems” and that rules applicable to payment systems are issued via regulations of the “Conseil de la Monnaie et du Crédit” (Monetary and Credit Council), indicating a regulatory/supervisory role rather than direct operation of the retail payment switch.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Upgraded. GIE Monétique's own governance page confirms the Bank of Algeria holds a designated seat on both the Conseil de Direction (governing board) and the Comité Opérationnel of the national payment-scheme operator — not merely a regulatory role. The 2020 activity report names the Bank of Algeria's Director-General for Payment Systems and Instruments as a Conseil de Direction member. Revised from "Regulatory Only" (2) to "Board Representation" (4).

Definition: Whether consumer protection legislation or regulations specifically address digital payment services, covering disclosure requirements, liability allocation for unauthorized transactions, error resolution procedures, and user rights.
Comments: Algeria has a legal framework for consumer protection in electronic commerce (including online contracting), via E-Commerce Law No. 18-05 dated 10 May 2018 (law discussed as providing mechanisms to protect the electronic consumer).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Upgraded. Bank of Algeria Instruction n°06-2025 (17 August 2025) introduces dedicated payment consumer protection rules beyond the general E-Commerce Law 18-05 previously cited: mandatory segregated escrow accounts for customer funds, bank guarantee/professional indemnity insurance, mandatory strong customer authentication, free access to balance/transaction history, and transaction receipts. This is dedicated, payment-specific consumer protection — revised from "Partial" (2) to "Yes" (3).

Comments: Algeria has general data protection legislation: Law No. 18-07 on protection of natural persons in personal data processing (cited by payment provider privacy notice as applicable Algerian law).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Law No. 18-07 remains the general data protection framework applicable to payment data; Instruction 06-2025 requires PSPs to meet data security/confidentiality obligations but does not create distinct statutory provisions specific to payment data. "General Data Protection Legislation" (2) is correct, not "Specific Payment Data Provisions" (3).

This is monthly/quarterly public disclosure, not merely annual reporting — revised from "Annual" (3) to "Monthly/Quarterly" (4).

Definition: Percentage of the adult population (15+ years) who have made at least one digital payment transaction through the instant payment system in the past 90 days, indicating active usage rather than just account ownership.
Comments: Digital payment usage estimate available from Global Findex (as presented in AfricaNenda SIIPS 2024 Algeria consumer research): proportion of population using digital payments over the past year (Findex 2021) is cited as 34% (about one-third). This maps to 20–49%.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Revised down. GIE Monétique's own 2025 bilan shows DZ Mob Pay — Algeria's instant payment system — had only 95,014 personal accounts by end-2025, a small fraction of the roughly 32 million adult population. Separately, an aggregator citing the newer Global Findex 2025 survey (fieldwork 2024) puts overall digital-payment adoption in Algeria at 13.1%, well below the 34% figure derived from the older 2021 Findex data used originally. Both point to <20% (1) rather than 20-49% (2); the FinStatGlobe figure could not be cross-checked directly against the primary World Bank Findex 2025 country report, so this is also flagged for human review.
